video_title: REACTING TO THE KAWHI LEONARD INVESTIGATION RESULTS

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' salary cap circumvention involved improper payments to Kawhi Leonard's associates
quotes.excerpt: Mr. Leonard through the conduct of Mr. Robertson on his behalf violated the circumvention rules

text_blocks.speaker: David Samson
text_blocks.text: Mr. Leonard through the conduct of Mr. Robertson on his behalf violated the circumvention rules by pressuring the Clippers to assist him in obtaining off-court income opportunities, successfully obtaining those opportunities and failing to reimburse payments by the Clippers for personal expenses.

text_blocks.speaker: Amin Elhassan
text_blocks.text: We could do a show just on those four lines.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: Private plane flights for players count toward the salary cap
quotes.excerpt: When we give that to a player in a contract, that is part of the contract

text_blocks.speaker: David Samson
text_blocks.text: When you have players and they want to take a private plane somewhere and you are in a capped league and owners have private planes and they want their family to go in different places, when we give that to a player in a contract, that is part of the contract. That is income to the player. It counts in our luxury tax. If a player gets 10 private plane flights, that is part of the calculation. You are not allowed, even in baseball, to have a player and then start doing all these things for the player and not disclosing it.

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo
text_blocks.text: It looks like in this report what Walk Tall is saying is Kawhi Leonard received tons of extra goodies from the Clippers and did not pay for them.

quotes.speaker: Amin Elhassan
quotes.summary_phrase: Players often receive extra benefits like game tickets that must be declared
quotes.excerpt: Players are allowed a certain amount of tickets, but sometimes players have big families

text_blocks.speaker: Amin Elhassan
text_blocks.text: Players are allowed a certain amount of tickets, but sometimes players have big families, sometimes they have lots of friends, and they are like, oh, I got 20 tickets every game. You know there is a tax for that, I mean. We have to keep track of what tickets we give to players because players have to declare that.

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo
text_blocks.text: We are starting with the deepest possible cut of this report. It is literally like the last thing that the NBA's investigation found.

quotes.speaker: Amin Elhassan
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers were penalized five first-round draft picks for salary cap violations
quotes.excerpt: The Clippers shall forfeit five first-round draft picks, one in each of the 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032, and 2033

text_blocks.speaker: Amin Elhassan
text_blocks.text: The penalties are: the Clippers shall forfeit five first-round draft picks, one in each of the 2029, 2030, 2031, 2032, and 2033 NBA drafts. That is a lot of picks. Clippers owner Steve Ballmer is suspended from all league and team activities for one year for knowingly seeking to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities, for approving a business deal that he knew was a precondition for Aspiration to enter into an endorsement agreement with Mr. Leonard, and for his failure to create conditions under which his organization abided by the NBA's circumvention rules.

text_blocks.speaker: David Samson
text_blocks.text: Five first-round picks is a lot, and we should point out that there are things in the collective bargaining agreement that outline punishments.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Ballmer's suspension means he cannot attend team games or owner meetings
quotes.excerpt: He can't be around the team. He can't go into his own arena

text_blocks.speaker: David Samson
text_blocks.text: When you are suspended from league and team activities, that means he doesn't go to owners' meetings. He can't be around the team. He can't go into his own arena. According to this punishment, he will be attending a total of zero games, zero practices, zero league-wide events, owners' meetings, etc. This is a full one-year suspension.

text_blocks.speaker: Pablo
text_blocks.text: Clippers president of business operations Gillian Zucker is suspended without pay for one year. Clippers president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank is suspended without pay for six months.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: Gillian Zucker's involvement in the scandal seems particularly problematic
quotes.excerpt: Gillian Zucker does not come off positively
quotes.quote: First blush at reading through the document, Gillian Zucker does not come off positively. The full statement in the document from Walk Tall Lipton says that she is suspended without pay for one year for being primarily and directly culpable for impermissible endorsement arrangements and for providing false and misleading statements to investigators. They made it a point, they even contrasted directly that the statements from Miss Zucker versus from Lawrence Frank, saying Lawrence Frank took culpability, he took accountability, he said it was on me, and he basically was up front, and meanwhile, Zucker basically either blamed subordinates or said did not remember or would give statements that were contradicting to other statements he had given.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' front office knew the rules and violated them anyway
quotes.excerpt: They knew the rules and violated them
quotes.quote: What Walk Tall found is that Zucker and Frank and Ballmer, they knew the rules. As Frank said and we said it in one of our shows, we showed Lawrence Frank answering a question from the podium. We know the rules. It turns out that Lawrence Frank indeed did know the rules and violated them. What Walk Tall also said in this report is that what Zucker did is that she also knew the rules and she not only misled the investigators, which is a big no-no when Ballmer had said it's full cooperation. That's not cooperating when you lie to the investigators. Number two, what Zucker did is she knew the rules and violated them in plain sight.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' punishment is significant because it involves a large fine and draft picks
quotes.excerpt: Steve Ballmer is going to write the check. The bigger issue for Steve Ballmer is not the 30 million
quotes.quote: I believe, and sources are telling me in the period after which 90 minutes, so this is very fresh, so I'll just say the collective bargaining agreement sets out a system for how you can dispute findings. It sets out a system for how players can, it sets out what owners can, it also sets out what owners can get fined. And it is my understanding that this is larger than a fine that you would normally see out of a CBA, out of a violation of salary cap circumvention. It is the largest of all time. And the evidence was so overwhelming, but a factor to me has to be that 30 million dollars is significant. Steve Ballmer is going to write the check. The bigger issue for Steve Ballmer is not the 30 million. It's the fact that from day one, when he sent you a statement that this is all provably false, he gives an interview to Ramona Shelburne day two that was all a lie. He doubles down on it, doubles down on it, and all the evidence collected by Walk Tall, 200,000 pages, all the 70 people interviewed, it all points to the fact that Ballmer led the salary cap circumvention campaign.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers have no arbitration process available to challenge the NBA's findings
quotes.excerpt: There is no arbitration process available to Steve Ballmer
quotes.quote: I have no idea how the Clippers released this statement because you fired the lawyers. There is no arbitration process available to Steve Ballmer. And having spoken to people within the league and my experience in baseball, there are exact things that go to arbitration, exact fights. This is not one of them, it's not allowed. The arbitration would be contained within the CBA and would be filed by the union on behalf of Kawhi. That's the big piece here is that the union and Kawhi said our bad. And now the Clippers are trying to activate an option that according to our understanding at this point at 6:27 p.m. Eastern, they actually need the union to activate to get to the system arbitrator.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The NBA and the team could agree to an arbitrator to settle disputes
quotes.excerpt: The NBA and a team could agree to an arbitrator to submit to an arbitration process
quotes.quote: The NBA and a team could agree to an arbitrator to submit to an arbitration process when there is a dispute between the league and the club. Both sides would have to agree to that. That's number one. Number two, what the Clippers say specifically is we intend to vigorously, I love when you use that adjective for no particular reason, that's as though sometimes you challenge findings in a not vigorous fashion, but they will vigorously challenge these findings. Where? The only avenue available to them is the court and not the podcast court, not the arbitration system, I'm talking about the court court, the real court. So all Steve Ballmer can announce is that we intend to sue the NBA because of their findings.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The NBA's investigation into Clippers' salary cap circumvention
quotes.excerpt: that is a huge burden for Steve Ballmer to try to get over in terms of successfully overturning
quotes.quote: There is a lawsuit and they are working on it right now and they are going to have to sue, I mean, maybe us, but certainly Adam Silver, the NBA. They tried to put Wachtell in there but I don't think that works at all. But in any case, that is a huge burden for Steve Ballmer to try to get over in terms of successfully overturning the punishment and the punishment is not Wachtell based, the NBA chose it. Wachtell doesn't say in here, I think so and so. The NBA chose it.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The suspension of AJ Hinch and Jeff Luhnow by the Astros
quotes.excerpt: the Astros result was a suspension of Hinch and a suspension of Luhnow, but Jim Crane then fired them
quotes.quote: Pablo, remember the Astros result was a suspension of Hinch and a suspension of Luhnow, but Jim Crane then fired them the next day. What I am waiting for and what I thought was coming before I read the Clipper statement, when I assumed the Clippers were acknowledging, I figured that they would fire Zuker tomorrow, the way the Astros fired Jeff Luhnow and AJ Hinch the next day. That she was suspended by the league and that they would just get fired. And I would expect that to still happen.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: Lawrence Frank's contract extension during the investigation
quotes.excerpt: Lawrence Frank got a big extension recently. A four-year extension. Went what month?
quotes.quote: Did Lawrence Frank get a big extension recently? Sure did. Sure did. A four-year extension. Went what month? December, I believe. The investigation is ongoing at this point. Lawrence Frank knows what happened, Ballmer knows what happened. He gets the extension. You can fire Frank, but you can still pay him out. You can fire him for cause and then you don't pay him, or you fire him without cause and you just pay him. And that could be the reward for Lawrence Frank for being the good soldier. He gets suspended for six months and then gets fired but paid that four-year extension.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The specific clause in the CBA regarding rational explanation
quotes.excerpt: cannot rationally be explained in the absence of conduct violative
quotes.quote: It is Article 13, Section 2, Part D: Violation of Section 2A to B above, may be proven by direct or circumstantial evidence, including but not limited to evidence that a player contract or any term or provision thereof, cannot rationally be explained in the absence of conduct violative. That is all we are talking about here guys. Give me a rational explanation for all of this.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' outside counsel's role in the investigation
quotes.excerpt: this effort was challenged by, among other things, the approach of the Clippers and their outside counsel
quotes.quote: This effort was challenged by, among other things, the approach of the Clippers and their outside counsel, who at times delayed in responding to request for information and operated in an adversarial or obfuscatory manner that slowed investigators' ability to gather the facts.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The consulting agreements between the Clippers and other companies
quotes.excerpt: None of Boingo, Dactronics and Lockton had commercial agreements with the Clippers
quotes.quote: In early June 2020, at the time of Miss Zuker's introductions, none of Boingo, Dactronics and Lockton had commercial agreements with the Clippers, but all three companies were in active discussions to provide business services to the team or its arena. Within weeks following the introductions, either before or on the same day as the companies signed endorsement agreements with Mr. Leonard, each company entered into a multi-million dollar consulting agreement with the Clippers.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The financial implications of the Clippers' consulting deals
quotes.excerpt: they also were getting more than that in because if they're getting an opportunity to be a part of Intuit's construction
quotes.quote: But they also were getting more than that in because if they're getting an opportunity to be a part of Intuit's construction, so don't say Dactronics got nothing, they got to do the Halo scoreboard. Don't say Boingo got nothing if they get to be the Wi-Fi provider. This is no small part of this finding by Wachtell, because this is what I have been describing to you on this show and on Nothing Personal, when you're building a stadium or a ballpark or you're doing any sort of business with sponsors, there's a lot of room to fudge numbers. There's a lot of room to hide money. There's a lot of opportunity to do things that may violate rules.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The causal relationship between the scoreboard deal and Leonard's endorsement
quotes.excerpt: there was an immediate causal relationship between Dactronics getting the business of the scoreboard and doing an endorsement deal
quotes.quote: What Wachtell found very clearly is that there was an immediate causal relationship between Dactronics getting the business of the scoreboard and doing an endorsement deal with Leonard. That is a violation on myriad levels.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The financial terms of the Clippers' endorsement agreements
quotes.excerpt: a senior Clippers executive specified the precise financial terms that the Clippers expected Dactronics to provide to Mr. Leonard
quotes.quote: In a call with a senior executive of Dactronics, a senior Clippers executive specified the precise financial terms that the Clippers expected Dactronics to provide to Mr. Leonard in the endorsement agreement: 3 million per year for two years.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' pressure on Dactronics to increase payments
quotes.excerpt: the Clippers executive told Dactronics that because the team had decided to increase the amount it would spend
quotes.quote: The Clippers executive told Dactronics that because the team had decided to increase the amount it would spend on the scoreboard, Dactronics should correspondingly increase the amount it would pay to Mr. Leonard. After some negotiation, and again based on its concern that failing to comply could jeopardize its business with the Clippers, Dactronics ultimately agreed to increase its second-year payment to Mr. Leonard by 2 million dollars.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' use of consulting agreements to pay Kawhi Leonard

quotes.quote: To underscore the point, the impetus to provide this additional 2 million dollar payment to Mr. Leonard did not come from Dactronics. Instead, it originated entirely from the Clippers.

Don't say Boingo got nothing if they get to be the Wi-Fi provider.

quotes.quote: The consultant told investigators that the Clippers had given him a 28 million dollar budget with which to address the forum's emissions, not the other way around.

There's a lot of opportunity to do things that may violate rules. And what Wachtell found very clearly is that there was an immediate causal relationship between Dactronics getting the business of the scoreboard and doing an endorsement deal with Leonard. That is a violation on myriad levels.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' use of consulting agreements to pay Kawhi Leonard
quotes.excerpt: Mr. Ballmer knowingly sought to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities
quotes.quote: Mr. Ballmer knowingly sought to help Mr. Leonard obtain off-court income opportunities and engaged in a significant act of facilitation through the forum agreement. Mr. Ballmer also failed to supervise his most senior business person while she systematically violated NBA rules and more generally permitted a culture in his organization that allowed for the initiation, facilitation, inducement and potential funding of multiple endorsement agreements between Mr. Leonard and team partners.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' use of consulting agreements to pay Kawhi Leonard
quotes.excerpt: Mr. Leonard, through his new agent, Harrison Gaines, issues statement
quotes.quote: Kawhi Leonard, through his new agent, Harrison Gaines, issues statement: 'Integrity and respect for this game are fundamental to who I am. I accept full responsibility for lapses in judgment by people within my inner circle and regret the distraction this situation has caused the fans and my family. I entered into my contract with the Clippers as well as the agreements in question in good faith, fully committed to fulfilling my obligations and with no knowledge of any one's part to circumvent the salary cap. For 15 years, my priority has been giving everything to my family, the game, and those I share the court with. As I return to Toronto, I am focused on what I can control, closing this chapter, and moving forward with a clean slate.'

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: The Clippers' use of consulting agreements to pay Kawhi Leonard
quotes.excerpt: the evidence supporting these findings is substantial
quotes.quote: The evidence supporting these findings is substantial. While it is possible that even more evidence will be uncovered as investigators continue to follow up on information that was recently received, the record as developed is more than sufficient to establish the rules violations described in the summary report.
